answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying each account to a costly, verifiable stake held on a ledge of locked funds: creating an identity requires locking value that is slashed if peers detect duplicate behaviour. A whisper of reputation then follows only proven work, so a new island of sockpuppets starts with no trust, no history, and no earnings. Attackers must pay separately for every identity while honest agents reuse one stake, making large-scale fakery unprofitable.
